snippet: Two drivers of Mercedes AMG cars have filed a class action lawsuit against the luxury car company, claiming that the AMG logo on their driver’s seat gets so hot that it literally brands them and causes burns. Gabriel Lahijani and Karendeep “Karina” Bath allege the front seats of certain Mercedes AMG vehicles have a design defect where the raised metallic AMG logo is “reasonably expected to contact an occupant’s upper back, neck, or shoulder,” according to the court document filed earlier this week in the U.S. District Court of California’s Western division. The plaintiffs want Mercedes to compensate them for any medical expenses, as well as any pain, suffering and emotional distress they can prove at trial. They also want Mercedes to pay for other owners to have the logo removed from their cars. Mercedes-Benz couldn’t be reached immediately for comment. Lahigani, a Los Angeles resident, had leased a new 2026 Mercedes-AMG E-Class vehicle from an authorized Mercedes-Benz dealership in Los Angeles, according to the suit. He reported receiving second-degree burns on his back on May 31, after entering his vehicle wearing a tank top. A board-certified dermatologist subsequently documented first- and second-degree burns, describing the injury as “AMG inscribed.” Roughly six weeks later, Bath, a Chatsworth, California resident, received similar burns allegedly from the logo design while wearing a sleeveless top. After parking her Mercedes-AMG vehicle in Los Angeles, Bath returned to the vehicle and entered the driver’s seat, the suit said. Her shoulder immediately touched the logo, causing a burning sensation. In the following days, a mark in the shape of the AMG logo “darkened and became visible on her skin, consistent with a thermal contact burn,” the lawsuit said. In December, Mercedes-Benz USA and parent company Daimer AG agreed to pay $149.6 million to settle allegations that the automaker secretly installed devices in hundreds of thousands of vehicles to pass emission tests, according to an announcement by a coalition of attorneys general. According to the coalition, between 2008 and 2016 the German automaker equipped more than 211,000 diesel passenger cars and vans with software devices that optimized emission controls during tests but reduced the controls during normal operations. headline: 35 taluks in Karnataka record less than 50% normal rainfall

snippet: Hubballi: As many as 35 taluks across the state have received less than 50% of their normal rainfall till August 7. Mysuru is the worst affected, with seven of its nine taluks clocking less than half their average rainfall. As many as 12 taluks in the state have recorded over 60% deficit rainfall. According to the data from the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre, of the 240 taluks, 61 received normal rainfall and 24 among them received higher than their normal rainfall. Sandur taluk in Ballari district recorded the state’s highest rainfall deficit at 76%, receiving just 56.3 mm against its normal 237.7 mm, followed by neighbouring Hosapete taluk in Vijayanagara district with nearly 75% deficit, while Gangavathi in Koppal received only 45 mm against its normal 168.6 mm. Karnataka faces 35% rain deficit; 25 districts record over 20% shortfall Vijayanagara, Hassan and Tumakuru districts each have three taluks that recorded more than 50% rainfall deficit, while Chamarajanagar, Kolar and Davangere have two taluks each with deficits exceeding 50%. Chikkamagaluru is the only taluk that received almost double its normal rainfall this year. In a normal year, it should have received 268.9 mm of rainfall; however, this year, the taluk received 420.5 mm, a 56% excess rainfall. By August 7, a total of 36 taluks in the state recorded over 1,000 mm of rainfall. Hebri in Udupi happens to be the taluk with highest rainfall in the state, with 2,462.1 mm rainfall. Chikkamagaluru’s Sringeri received second highest rainfall this season with 2,276.5 mm. Udupi’s seven taluks and Dakshina Kannada’s nine taluks received in excess of 1,500 mm of rainfall so far this monsoon. A total of 11 taluks in Malnad and coastal districts received over 2,000 mm of rainfall.

headline: Report calls for scientific assessment of sloth bear population in India
triage_reason: Report calls for scientific assessment of sloth bear population in India.
snippet: Bengaluru: Sloth bears are distributed across 23 states in India with available assessments indicating that central and western India constitute their major strongholds, says a new report. The ‘Conservation Status Report of Sloth Bear Sanctuaries in India’ by the Wildlife Institute of India noted that population estimates remain fragmented due to various reasons. India supports four species of bears: sloth bear, Himalayan brown bear, Asiatic black bear and Malayan sun bear. Among them the sloth bear is unique because it is endemic to the sub-continent. “Sloth bears face multiple conservation challenges, primarily driven by habitat loss, fragmentation and human-induced pressures. Increasing land-use change outside protected areas has resulted in degraded habitats and disrupted connectivity. Additionally, poaching for body parts, including claws, bile and meat has intensified over recent decades,” the report said, adding that the animal has been listed under Schedule 1 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Sloth bear strays into Gondia neighbourhoods, evades capture; forest guard injured during rescue bid It said though distributed widely, the species enjoys protection mainly due to the protected areas of India. It hailed the five bear-specific sanctuaries for playing a crucial role in strengthening conservation efforts. Daroji, Gudekote and Arasikere sanctuaries in Karnataka as well as the Jessore and Ratanmahal sanctuaries in Gujarat. “Although relatively small landscapes within human-dominated areas, these sanctuaries encompass critical dry deciduous, thorn and scrub forest ecosystems that provide essential resources, such as denning sites, seasonal food availability and refuge,” it added. The report referred to old studies about bear population and underlined the need for systematic surveys in the states to strengthen state-level population monitoring.

snippet: Bengaluru: The Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL) has started commercialising the surplus 'dark fibre' available on its 6,119-km Optical Ground Wire (OPGW) fibre network and this is expected to generate substantial long-term revenue. Under this, KPTCL will retain 12 out of its 24 optical fibre pairs for its captive grid communication requirements and lease the other 12 fibre pairs to licensed telecom service providers, data network companies and other authorised service providers on commercial basis. Energy Minister K J George said this will promote growth of high-speed digital connectivity. "KPTCL is no longer just a power transmission utility; it is playing a significant role in building state's digital infrastructure. Commercialising the surplus dark fibre is an excellent example of optimising public assets. Besides creating a sustainable long-term revenue stream for KPTCL, this will accelerate growth of high-speed digital connectivity and digital economy,” he said. KPTCL strengthens cybersecurity measures in Bengaluru The project is set to generate approximately Rs 130 crore in fixed revenue for KPTCL over the 15-year contract period. "KPTCL's OPGW network forms digital backbone of our power transmission system. By retaining capacity for secure grid communication and commercialising surplus dark fibre, we are unlocking value of public infrastructure. This will give reliable fibre connectivity to telecom operators, data centres and next generation of digital communication networks," said Ramprasat Manohar V, MD, KPTCL.

Kumaraswamy said that the judgement, delivered by the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court on July 29, laid bare several irregularities in the execution of the NICE project. “The court has raised several issues pertaining to the project. NICE failed to adhere to the terms of the framework agreement. The court has framed the issue in serious terms. What more justification does the government need to take over the project,” asked Kumaraswamy. The Union Minister claimed that vested interests had profited from the land acquired for the NICE project. “More than 20,000 acres were acquired for a land bank. Thousands of farmers were left without a means of livelihood as a result,” rued Kumaraswamy. The Union Minister also took exception to NICE issuing a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) to Sobha Developers for the construction of a building at Hosakerehalli in Bengaluru. “I want to ask the Chief Minister who benefits from this agreement? What authority does NICE have to issue an NOC to Sobha Developers? How was the land offered to the real estate company,” asked Kumaraswamy. BJP, JD(S) join hands against Congress; plan united padayatra over Bidadi township Kumaraswamy said the BJP would support a foot march (padayatra) led by JD(S) youth wing president Nikhil Kumaraswamy from Byramangala to Freedom Park in Bengaluru. The march starts on Sunday morning. Kumaraswamy will flag off the march along with BJP leaders. Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka said the BJP workers had been asked to join the march and that the two parties would jointly protest against the project both inside and outside the legislature. They also plan district-level protests. Ashoka said a 10-member coordination committee would be formed to ensure greater coordination ahead of elections.
